B1:
Cause: Touched fires once per touching body part and many times per contact (each limb, re-touches) in the same frames; Destroy doesn't stop handlers already queued, and with Deferred signals several fire before the part is gone. So 3-5 touches each grant 10.
Fix: debounce with a guard set before any yield, and destroy after:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if collected then return end
  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  local hum = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  collected = true
  part.CanTouch = false
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For per-player respawning pickups use a table of players with cooldown instead of one bool.
B2:
With StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player; far parts of Workspace aren't streamed in yet (and can stream out), so the client-side path workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel.Door errors when Door (or a parent) doesn't exist on the client. It's fine near spawn because that area is streamed.
Fix 1: Use CollectionService tags: tag doors "Door"; on the client do `for _, d in CS:GetTagged("Door") do hook(d) end` + `CS:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door"):Connect(hook)` (and InstanceRemovedSignal to clean up). Handles streaming in/out.
Fix 2: Make the Hotel model persistent/atomic: Model.ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (arrives as a unit) or Persistent (always present), then WaitForChild along the path (WaitForChild with timeout); or handle Touched on the server instead (server sees everything).
Avoid plain long WaitForChild chains without timeouts on non-persistent content (infinite yield).
B3:
Bugs:
1. Always returns PurchaseGranted, even when pcall failed -> charged, nothing saved. Must return NotProcessedYet on failure.
2. No idempotency: no record of info.PurchaseId, so Roblox retries (or a timeout/rejoin) grant again -> double coins.
3. GetAsync+SetAsync is a non-atomic read-modify-write; another server/session save can overwrite it or race. Use UpdateAsync (or session-locked profile).
4. plr can be nil (player left) -> plr.UserId errors inside pcall -> still returns Granted. Use info.PlayerId, or return NotProcessedYet if player absent and you grant in-session.
5. ProductId not checked - any product gives 100 coins; also saving directly bypasses the in-memory session data, which the session save later overwrites.
Correct behaviour: look up handler by info.ProductId; if PurchaseId already recorded -> PurchaseGranted; otherwise grant+record PurchaseId in one UpdateAsync (or session profile then save); return PurchaseGranted only after it succeeds, else NotProcessedYet.
B4:
Remotes serialize arguments: tables are copied as plain data, so metatables are stripped -> the client gets {Name="Rifle", Ammo=30} with no __index, and w:Fire() is nil. Functions are never sent either. Instances are sent as references, but only if they exist on the receiving side; ServerStorage isn't replicated to clients, so the Muzzle arrives as nil.
Fix: send plain data (e.g. {Name=..., Ammo=...} or an id) and rebuild the object on the client from a shared ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage: `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` / Weapon.new(data). For the part, put it (or a clone) somewhere replicated (ReplicatedStorage/Workspace) before firing, or send an identifier and have the client fetch its own copy from ReplicatedStorage. (Also mixed/sparse table keys and non-string keys may be lost.)
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the direction vector including length, not a unit direction. Passing .Unit makes the ray only 1 stud long, so it hits nothing unless the target is within 1 stud. It also likely hits the shooter's own character/gun at the origin.
Fix:
```lua
local MAX = 500
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * MAX
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
(Or use target - origin directly if you want to stop at the target.)
B6:
When the last player leaves, the server starts shutting down; PlayerRemoving's async SetAsync may still be in flight (or not yet started) when the process closes, so the save is lost. Also SetAsync can fail with no retry.
Fix: use game:BindToClose to save every remaining player and yield until those saves finish (the server waits up to ~30 s total for BindToClose callbacks). Track in-flight saves so PlayerRemoving and BindToClose don't double-save, and wait for pending ones:
```lua
game:BindToClose(function()
  if game:GetService("RunService"):IsStudio() then task.wait(1) end
  local pending = 0
  for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
    pending += 1
    task.spawn(function() savePlayer(p) pending -= 1 end)
  end
  while pending > 0 do task.wait() end
end)
```
Use UpdateAsync with pcall/retry, autosave periodically so little is lost anyway.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: {[Player]: number} = {}

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, ...)
  local now = os.clock()
  local t = lastUse[player]
  if t and now - t < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
  lastUse[player] = now
  -- validate any args here (types, NaN, ranges)
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
```

B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DSS = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DSS:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local GEMS100 = 123456

local handlers = {[GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
  if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on rejoin
  local ok, err = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, "Player_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
    data = data or {Gems = 0}
    data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
    if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
    handler(data)
    data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time() -- trim old entries periodically
    return data
  end)
  if not ok then
    warn("Receipt failed", err)
    return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
  end
  -- refresh in-memory session/leaderstats from saved data here
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Set ProcessReceipt once; Granted only after the durable write; idempotent per PurchaseId. If you use a session-locked profile, write into that profile and save instead of a separate UpdateAsync.

```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current: Tween?

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = HIDDEN
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = SHOWN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = HIDDEN})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```
(AnchorPoint 0.5,0.5 assumed for centering. Optionally use EasingDirection.In for the close.)
B10:
```lua
local RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" then return end
  if targetPos ~= targetPos then return end -- NaN guard (component NaN check)
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local dir = offset.Unit * RANGE
  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local targetHum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if targetHum and targetHum.Health > 0 then
    targetHum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
  end
end
```
Call from a validated remote with a fire-rate cooldown; server does the ray, not the client.
B11:
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns: {[BasePart]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local model = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
  end)
end

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end

for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end
CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
```
Removed signal also fires when the part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.

B13:
(a) Buying: client -> server RemoteEvent (e.g. BuyItem:FireServer(itemId)) or a RemoteFunction invoked by the client if it needs a result (success/reason). All validation lives on the server: item exists, server-side price, the server-held balance, cooldown; the server deducts coins and grants the sword. The authoritative balance lives in server player data (session/profile), never on the client.
(b) UI update: server -> client RemoteEvent (CoinsChanged:FireClient(player, newBalance)), or just replicate via leaderstats/attribute (player:SetAttribute("Coins", n)) and have the client listen with GetAttributeChangedSignal.
Why not server->client RemoteFunction (InvokeClient): the server yields until the client answers; an exploiter can never return (hang the server thread forever), error, or return junk; if the client leaves it errors. Server must never depend on client responses. One-way RemoteEvents/replicated values don't have this problem.
B14:
Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData / GetJoinData().TeleportData) travels through the client, so it can be spoofed and is not secure; it's also lost if the teleport fails or the player joins the match place another way, and has a size limit. Fine for non-authoritative hints (chosen map, party id, cosmetic loadout preference).
DataStores: authoritative, persistent, secure; the coin balance should live here (session-locked profile). Save and release the lock before teleport; the destination loads it (retry briefly if the lock is still held). Slower and costs request budget.
MemoryStores (HashMap/SortedMap): fast, server-only, expiring cross-server state - good for transient match state like the chosen loadout or a match reservation keyed by UserId with a short TTL.
Choice: coins in the DataStore profile (save before teleport, load in match place); loadout in the profile too or in a MemoryStore HashMap with TTL; teleport data only for non-sensitive hints (e.g. match id), validated on arrival against the server-side source.
B15:
Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): each Script is a separate VM thread/ connections set, duplicated code that must be edited in 610 places, harder memory/perf, copies drift, poor with streaming (scripts in streamed parts on client), and spawned clones bring their own scripts.
Tag-driven: tag instances with CollectionService ("Door", "Pickup", "Turret"), one server Script (or module per type) per tag: iterate CollectionService:GetTagged(tag) for existing instances, connect GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag) for newly spawned/cloned or streamed-in instances, and GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag) to disconnect/clean up (Janitor/Trove per instance). Per-instance config via attributes (e.g. Damage, Range). Turrets can share one Heartbeat loop updating all active turrets (throttled), rather than 60 loops. On the client (with StreamingEnabled), the same tag signals fire as instances stream in/out, so client visuals bind/unbind automatically. Structure: ServerScriptService/Systems/DoorSystem, PickupSystem, TurretSystem (ModuleScripts started by one bootstrap), shared config in ReplicatedStorage.
B16:
Ownership: give the driver network ownership of the car (VehicleSeat occupant -> server calls part:SetNetworkOwner(driverPlayer) on the chassis when they sit; SetNetworkOwner(nil) or auto when they leave). Otherwise input-to-physics latency makes driving feel laggy. Unoccupied cars stay server-owned (or auto).
Risk: the owning client simulates the car's physics and the server accepts it, so an exploiter can teleport the car, exceed top speed, fly, fling other players/cars, or cross the finish instantly.
Server must still validate: position/speed plausibility each step (max speed, acceleration, no teleports - compare with last positions), checkpoint order and lap timing (finish only after all checkpoints in order, min lap time), collisions/damage results, ownership only to the actual seated driver, and anything granting rewards (race results, currency) computed on the server. Revert ownership/reset the car or kick on violations.
B17:
Use UnreliableRemoteEvent for high-frequency, latest-value-only data like aim direction/position: unordered, no retransmission, no queueing behind lost packets, so less bandwidth/queue pressure.
Constraints: packets can be dropped or arrive out of order; payload per call is small (~900 bytes; larger is dropped); no guaranteed delivery.
Handling: send only latest state (idempotent snapshots), include a sequence number/timestamp and drop older ones, interpolate on receivers; reduce the rate (e.g. 10-20 Hz, or only on meaningful change/delta threshold), compress (e.g. buffer, quantized angles/Vector2 pitch-yaw instead of CFrames); keep important events (shots fired, hits, purchases) on reliable RemoteEvents; still validate on server (rate-limit, sanity-check positions). Also prefer letting character replication handle position rather than resending it.
B18:
Parallel Luau: put the NPC logic in scripts under Actor instances (e.g. split 200 NPCs across N Actors, ~cores x 2-4, or one Actor per NPC group). Each Actor's script connects RunService.Heartbeat with ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize()) and does the read-only work in parallel: raycasts (workspace:Raycast is safe in parallel), path scoring, target selection, math. Then task.synchronize() (or a later serial phase) to apply results: move humanoids, set properties, fire remotes, damage. Communicate via Actor:SendMessage/BindToMessage(Parallel) or SharedTable.
Limits: in the parallel phase you can't write most instance properties or call non-thread-safe APIs (writes only to instances in your own Actor's subtree for some; check thread-safety tags); no yielding inside desynchronized code; modules required in each Actor are separate copies (no shared Lua state; use SharedTable for shared data); data passed via messages is copied; overhead of sync/desync per frame. Also reduce work: stagger NPC updates across frames, LOD by distance, cache paths (ComputeAsync not every frame).
B19:
Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Settings: StreamingMinRadius ~64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius ~1024 default (lower, e.g. 256-512, for mobile memory), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic (stream out to save memory), StreamingIntegrityMode = Default or PauseOutsideLoadedArea (pause character if area not loaded). Use Model.ModelStreamingMode: Atomic for models that must arrive whole, Persistent only for few always-needed things (sparingly), PersistentPerPlayer + Player:AddReplicationFocus as needed; use Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting a player.
Scripts: client code must not assume instances exist: replace direct paths with WaitForChild (with timeout) on non-persistent content, or better CollectionService tags with GetInstanceAddedSignal/RemovedSignal to bind and unbind as content streams in/out; handle nil and instances disappearing (stream out); server scripts are unaffected (server has everything). Also reduce asset sizes/textures, use LOD (Model.LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh) for far models.
B20:
Cause: 80 players x SetAsync every 5 s = ~960 writes/min, above the write budget (~300 + 20 x CCU per experience per minute since mid-2026; per-server limits are similar ~60 + 10 x players) and above the per-key limit (a key can be written about once every 6 s). Requests queue; when a key's queue fills (30) further requests fail with error 302 (queue full), so saves are dropped; SetAsync also overwrites blindly.
Better design: keep data in a server-side session cache (profile); save with UpdateAsync (session lock) only on a slow autosave interval (~60-120 s, staggered/jittered per player), on PlayerRemoving, on important events (purchases - immediately via receipt flow), and in BindToClose. Skip saves when the data hasn't changed (dirty flag). Check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before writing and back off on errors with retries. Use ProfileStore/ProfileService-style libraries.

B22:
Three core instances:
- InputContext: a group of actions that can be enabled/disabled together; properties Enabled, Priority, Sink.
- InputAction: a named action with a Type (Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D, Direction3D, ViewportPosition).
- InputBinding: child of an action mapping a device input to it - KeyCode (keyboard/gamepad/mouse), UIButton (a GuiButton for touch), modifiers (PrimaryModifier/SecondaryModifier), Scale, composite directions.
Signalling: a Bool action fires Pressed and Released; every action fires StateChanged(newState); you can poll InputAction:GetState() (needed for analog values each frame); Fire() can trigger it from code.
Menu precedence: put menu actions in their own InputContext with a higher Priority than the default player-scripts context and Sink = true, and enable it while the menu is open; it consumes those inputs so lower-priority contexts (default movement/camera controls) don't receive them. Disable the context when closing.
B23:
Roblox's UI Styling (style sheets) system applies CSS-like rules to GuiObjects.
Instances:
- StyleSheet: container of rules (and token attributes).
- StyleRule: a Selector (class names e.g. ".Primary" from GuiObject tags, instance class e.g. "TextButton", names "#Close", pseudo-state ":hover"/":press" via GuiState, child/descendant combinators, @queries) plus properties set via SetProperty/SetProperties; Priority; rules can nest.
- StyleLink: placed in a ScreenGui/LayerCollector, its StyleSheet property links a sheet to that UI tree (one sheet per tree).
- StyleDerive: lets a sheet inherit rules/tokens from another sheet (base theme -> overrides).
- StyleQuery: conditional rules (MaxSize, PreferredInput etc.) - beta.
How styles reach UI: StyleLink connects the sheet; matching rules apply to the GuiObjects in that tree, re-evaluated when tags/state change; properties set directly in code can conflict, so don't set the same property both ways.
Tokens: define attributes on a token StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor = Color3) and reference them in rules as "$PrimaryColor"; swapping/deriving the token sheet re-themes the whole UI (light/dark).
B24:
Method: facial age estimation via the Roblox app (selfie video processed by vendor Persona, images deleted after); 13+ can alternatively use ID verification; parental controls can correct a child's age.
Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+.
Restriction: once checked, users can chat only with their own age group and adjacent groups (e.g. 13-15 with 9-12 and 16-17); under-16s can't chat with adults (18+). Trusted Connections (for 13+ users who know each other) can widen this. Users who haven't completed the check lose access to chat. Under-9s have chat off by default and need parental consent. Rollout: announced Nov 2025, enforced in some countries Dec 2025, globally Jan 2026. Developers get no API exposing a user's age group; don't make gameplay depend on chat.
